===== FILE: .github/workflows/extraction-eval.yml
==============================================================================

name: Extraction Golden-Set Exam (release-blocking)

# KAIZEN §M7 / R-013: no extraction change ships without golden-set exam
# evidence. Design v4 (r9→r12 evaluator doctrine, founder-directed
# personal-repo constraints):
#
#   * This PR-triggered job carries NO SECRETS. The secret-bearing exam
#     runs only in extraction-exam-dispatch.yml — manual, maintainer-
#     dispatched, default-branch harness only.
#   * TRUST PLACEMENT: every trust decision below executes from the BASE
#     checkout. The subject (PR head) contributes only inert data — its
#     prompt text and routed-model id, lifted by BASE AST extractors that
#     never import or execute subject code.
#   * SURFACE CLASSIFICATION: prompt-swap evidence can only certify what
#     the attended exam actually ran. A PR whose extraction-surface diff
#     is confined to SUBJECT-CERTIFIABLE files (ai/prompts.py and
#     tools/routing_data.py — both PURE DATA modules, enforced by the
#     extractors: nothing executable may appear in them) can go green
#     with binding evidence. A PR that changes HARNESS code (runner,
#     provider, scoring, golden set, extractors, verifier, these
#     workflows) FAILS here with split instructions: harness changes
#     merge first through the mandatory evaluator gate, then subjects are
#     certified against the merged harness (the PR #11 bootstrap
#     pattern). The exam never certifies code it did not run.
#   * BASE-OWNED TRIGGER (r19): this workflow runs on pull_request_target,
#     so GitHub executes the DEFAULT BRANCH's copy of this file — a PR
#     that edits this workflow does not change what runs against it. That
#     closes the last tamper surface mechanically. pull_request_target is
#     safe here precisely because of the rule above: no subject code is
#     ever executed — both trust-path checkouts below are pinned SHAs,
#     all executed code is base's, and the subject contributes files read
#     as data. Permissions are read-only; no secret beyond the ambient
#     read token is requested.
#
# Bootstrap honesty (r11): on the PR that ARMS this gate, this check is
# necessarily red — no trusted attended producer exists on the default
# branch until that PR merges. That arming PR merges with this one check
# red under explicit human review (precedent: PR #11).

on:
  pull_request_target:
    paths:
      - "ai/**"
      - "worker/ai_models.py"
      - "worker/ai_extract.py"
      - "tools/__init__.py"
      - "tools/model_router.py"
      - "tools/routing_data.py"
      - "tools/pure_data.py"
      - "tools/golden_lint.py"
      - "tools/trust_gate.py"
      - "tests/test_golden_exam.py"
      - "tools/verify_exam_evidence.py"
      - "tools/extract_prompt_text.py"
      - "tools/extract_routed_model.py"
      - "tools/classify_extraction_surface.py"
      - "tools/authenticate_certification_record.py"
      - ".github/workflows/extraction-eval.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/extraction-exam-dispatch.yml"
      # Dependency surface (r24/r26): the exam runs under these installed
      # packages, so changing them changes extraction behavior — a dep
      # bump is a harness change and requires fresh exam evidence.
      - "worker/requirements.txt"
      - "worker/requirements.lock"

concurrency:
  # PR number, not github.ref (r24 nit): under pull_request_target the
  # ref is the BASE branch, which would serialize/cancel unrelated PRs'
  # evaluations against the same base.
  group: extraction-eval-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  golden-exam:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read      # to find the attended run + download its report artifact
    steps:
      # TRUSTED code: the base branch the PR merges into.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3, r9/r26 nit): pins must be VERIFIED upstream SHAs, and this sandboxed session cannot read actions/* to verify — tag stays until a networked session or the founder confirms the SHAs
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: base
          persist-credentials: false

      # SUBJECT: checked out only as FILES to read data from — nothing in
      # this checkout is executed by the trust path below.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3, r9/r26 nit): pins must be VERIFIED upstream SHAs, and this sandboxed session cannot read actions/* to verify — tag stays until a networked session or the founder confirms the SHAs
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          path: subject
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3) — same constraint as checkout above
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install worker deps (for the BASE verifier's threshold imports)
        # --no-deps against the FULL transitive lock (r26): the verifier's
        # own environment resolves from exactly the set the evidence binds.
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install --no-deps -r base/worker/requirements.lock

      - name: Classify the extraction-surface diff (harness code cannot ride a prompt-swap exam)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${BASE_SHA:?base sha unresolved — failing closed}"
          : "${HEAD_SHA:?head sha unresolved — failing closed}"
          # Compare via the API (the checkouts are credential-less by design,
          # so a git fetch here would have no auth). The compare API caps the
          # file list at 300 entries; a bigger diff fails closed in the
          # classifier.
          : "${GH_TOKEN:?GH_TOKEN missing — cannot verify evidence, failing closed}"
          curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" > compare.json
          # BASE-owned classifier, moved out of an inline heredoc (PR #36 r2):
          # as a file it is unit-testable — the CLASSIFIER the charter's
          # enumerated golden-exam exception keys on now has its own tests
          # (tests/test_classify_extraction_surface.py) — and this shell is
          # simple enough for tools/workflow_env_lint.py to verify. The first
          # call is the blocking refusal gate (harness code cannot ride a
          # prompt-swap exam); the --print calls re-run the same full
          # classification and emit one flag each for the later steps.
          python3 -I base/tools/classify_extraction_surface.py compare.json --base-dir base --subject-dir subject
          RECORD_CHANGED="$(python3 -I base/tools/classify_extraction_surface.py compare.json --base-dir base --subject-dir subject --print record-changed)"
          SURFACE_BEYOND_RECORD="$(python3 -I base/tools/classify_extraction_surface.py compare.json --base-dir base --subject-dir subject --print surface-beyond-record)"
          echo "RECORD_CHANGED=$RECORD_CHANGED" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "SURFACE_BEYOND_RECORD=$SURFACE_BEYOND_RECORD" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Lift subject expectations as data (BASE extractors, subject files)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -I base/tools/extract_prompt_text.py subject/ai/prompts.py > subject_prompt.txt
          EXPECT_PROMPT_SHA="$(python3 -I -c "import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open('subject_prompt.txt','rb').read()).hexdigest())")"
          EXPECT_MODEL="$(python3 -I base/tools/extract_routed_model.py subject/tools/routing_data.py)"
          if ! [[ "$EXPECT_MODEL" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::subject routed model is not a plausible model id (fail closed)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # Harness-version bindings (r22): the evidence must have been
          # minted by THIS golden set and scorer (base's), not an older one.
          EXPECT_GOLDEN_SHA="$(python3 -I -c "import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(open('base/ai/golden/golden_set_v1.jsonl','rb').read()).hexdigest())")"
          # The same single-source function the runner used, run from BASE
          # (r23: the manifest covers every file executing during a run).
          # Under -I the cwd is NOT on sys.path (that is the point), so the
          # BASE checkout root — a trusted directory — is inserted
          # EXPLICITLY for this one repo-local import (stage-4 r2: the
          # blanket -I would otherwise break this import at runtime).
          EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA="$(cd base && python3 -I -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from ai.golden_exam import compute_harness_sha; print(compute_harness_sha())")"
          echo "EXPECT_PROMPT_SHA=$EXPECT_PROMPT_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "EXPECT_MODEL=$EXPECT_MODEL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "EXPECT_GOLDEN_SHA=$EXPECT_GOLDEN_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA=$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # ---- Certification-record authentication (evaluator, PR #36 r2/r3) ----
      # Stage 1 of the gate→record→re-lock bootstrap (r3: the gate must
      # land BEFORE the record — under pull_request_target only a MERGED
      # copy of this step can authenticate anything, so a record riding in
      # the same PR as its authenticator would enter unverified). The
      # offline trust_gate re-lock (stage 3) will prove a committed record
      # stays complete, PASSED, threshold-passing, and hash-bound — but
      # offline code cannot prove a record is REAL. This step is the
      # online half: any PR that changes
      # ai/golden/CERTIFIED_HARNESS.json must present a record whose run_id
      # is an actual successful maintainer-dispatched attended run on the
      # default branch, whose artifact zip hashes to the recorded digest,
      # and whose uploaded exam-report.json agrees with every recorded
      # field — then the report passes the SAME evidence verifier as the
      # head-bound path. Base-owned (pull_request_target): the PR cannot
      # edit the copy that judges its record. A record can only enter the
      # tree authenticated; forging one is now a red check, not a green.
      - name: Authenticate the changed certification record against its attended run (BASE code, fail closed)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${RECORD_CHANGED:?classification step did not run — failing closed}"
          if [ "$RECORD_CHANGED" != "1" ]; then
            echo "certification record unchanged in this PR — nothing to authenticate"
            exit 0
          fi
          : "${GH_TOKEN:?GH_TOKEN missing — cannot authenticate the record, failing closed}"
          : "${DEFAULT_BRANCH:?default branch unresolved — failing closed}"
          : "${EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA:?expectations step did not run — failing closed}"
          : "${EXPECT_MODEL:?expectations step did not run — failing closed}"
          cd base
          RECORD="../subject/ai/golden/CERTIFIED_HARNESS.json"
          # BASE-owned authenticator (tools/authenticate_certification_record.py,
          # unit-tested): every subcommand re-runs the FULL structural + base-
          # binding validation first — no subcommand is a lighter gate. The
          # printed fields are shape-validated (digits / 40-hex), so the
          # captures below are shell-safe; under set -e any rejection kills
          # this step.
          REC_RUN_ID="$(python3 -I tools/authenticate_certification_record.py field "$RECORD" run_id --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA" --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL")"
          REC_SUBJECT_SHA="$(python3 -I tools/authenticate_certification_record.py field "$RECORD" subject_sha --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA" --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL")"
          api() { curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" "$@"; }
          api "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$REC_RUN_ID" > run.json
          api "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$REC_RUN_ID/artifacts" > artifacts.json
          ART_URL="$(python3 -I tools/authenticate_certification_record.py run "$RECORD" run.json artifacts.json --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA" --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL" --default-branch "$DEFAULT_BRANCH")"
          # Evidence is untrusted DATA (r15): downloaded and extracted in an
          # isolated temp dir, never into the trusted checkout; the zip must
          # hash to the recorded digest and contain exactly one
          # exam-report.json, and every recorded metric must agree with it.
          TMPD="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$TMPD"' EXIT
          api -L -o "$TMPD/report.zip" "$ART_URL"
          python3 -I tools/authenticate_certification_record.py report "$RECORD" "$TMPD/report.zip" "$TMPD" --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA" --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL"
          # Full independent evidence verification — the SAME verifier and
          # bindings as the head-bound path, anchored to the record's
          # default-branch subject commit. EXPECT_* are subject-derived and
          # equal base's for a record-only PR; a PR that pairs a record with
          # a prompt change fails here BY DESIGN: records land in their own
          # PR, after the harness they certify has merged.
          python3 -I tools/verify_exam_evidence.py "$TMPD/exam-report.json" \
            --subject-sha "$REC_SUBJECT_SHA" \
            --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL" \
            --expect-prompt-sha256 "$EXPECT_PROMPT_SHA" \
            --expect-golden-sha256 "$EXPECT_GOLDEN_SHA" \
            --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA"
          echo "certification record AUTHENTICATED against attended run $REC_RUN_ID"

      - name: Verify attended exam evidence binds to this head (BASE verifier, fail closed)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${SURFACE_BEYOND_RECORD:?classification step did not run — failing closed}"
          if [ "$SURFACE_BEYOND_RECORD" != "1" ]; then
            # Record-ONLY PR: nothing extraction-behavioral changed at this
            # head, so no attended run can (or should) bind to it — the
            # record itself was authenticated by the fail-closed steps above
            # against the default-branch commit its exam actually ran on.
            echo "only the certification record changed on the extraction surface — head-bound exam evidence not applicable"
            exit 0
          fi
          : "${HEAD_SHA:?head sha unresolved — failing closed}"
          cd base
          : "${GH_TOKEN:?GH_TOKEN missing — cannot verify evidence, failing closed}"
          api() { curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" "$@"; }
          # Evidence tempdirs live under one root with a cleanup trap
          # (r-hygiene): nothing evidence-related is left on disk after
          # the step, success or failure.
          TMPD_ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$TMPD_ROOT"' EXIT
          # 50-run window (r15/r16 nits): fail-closed either way. OPERATOR
          # NOTE, prominent by design: if many exams ran since yours, valid
          # evidence can age out of this window — the remedy is always ONE
          # re-dispatch with the same subject_sha/model; the gate never
          # skips or degrades.
          # Only runs whose head_branch IS the default branch count (r18
          # blocker): a branch dispatch executes the BRANCH's copy of the
          # attended workflow — guard stripped, artifacts forgeable. The
          # trusted-harness guarantee lives in this filter as much as in
          # the workflow's own ref guard.
          RUN_IDS="$(api "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/extraction-exam-dispatch.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&status=success&per_page=50" | python3 -I -c "
          import json, os, sys
          default = os.environ['DEFAULT_BRANCH']
          runs = json.load(sys.stdin).get('workflow_runs') or []
          print(' '.join(str(r['id']) for r in runs if r.get('head_branch') == default))
          ")"
          if [ -z "$RUN_IDS" ]; then
            echo "::error::No successful ATTENDED exam runs exist at all. A maintainer must dispatch 'Extraction Golden-Set Exam — attended run' on the default branch with subject_sha=$HEAD_SHA and the subject's routed model ($EXPECT_MODEL), then re-run this check (fail closed)."
            exit 1
          fi
          FOUND=""
          for RUN_ID in $RUN_IDS; do
            # Evidence is untrusted DATA (r15): extract into a fresh isolated
            # temp dir, never into the trusted checkout — a hostile archive
            # must not be able to overwrite the code that judges it. The
            # archive must contain exactly one member named exam-report.json.
            TMPD="$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPD_ROOT")"
            ART_URL="$(api "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/artifacts" | python3 -I -c "import json,sys; arts=json.load(sys.stdin).get('artifacts') or []; hits=[a for a in arts if a['name'].startswith('golden-exam-report-')]; print(hits[0]['archive_download_url'] if hits else '')")"
            [ -z "$ART_URL" ] && continue
            api -L -o "$TMPD/report.zip" "$ART_URL" || continue
            python3 -I - "$TMPD" <<'PYZ' || continue
          import sys, zipfile
          tmpd = sys.argv[1]
          with zipfile.ZipFile(tmpd + "/report.zip") as z:
              if z.namelist() != ["exam-report.json"]:
                  print("::warning::artifact is not exactly one exam-report.json — skipping this run")
                  sys.exit(1)
              z.extract("exam-report.json", tmpd)
          PYZ
            [ -f "$TMPD/exam-report.json" ] || continue
            if python3 -I tools/verify_exam_evidence.py "$TMPD/exam-report.json" \
                 --subject-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
                 --expect-model "$EXPECT_MODEL" \
                 --expect-prompt-sha256 "$EXPECT_PROMPT_SHA" \
                 --expect-golden-sha256 "$EXPECT_GOLDEN_SHA" \
                 --expect-harness-sha256 "$EXPECT_HARNESS_SHA"; then
              FOUND="$RUN_ID"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "$FOUND" ]; then
            echo "::error::No attended exam evidence binds to head SHA $HEAD_SHA with the subject's routed model ($EXPECT_MODEL) and exact prompt. Dispatch 'Extraction Golden-Set Exam — attended run' on the default branch with subject_sha=$HEAD_SHA and model=$EXPECT_MODEL, then re-run this check (fail closed)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "attended evidence accepted from run $FOUND"

      - name: Golden-set structural + contamination lint (BASE-owned code over SUBJECT data; blocking)
        # r14: lint that runs from the subject checkout can be weakened by
        # the very PR it judges. tools/golden_lint.py is base code reading
        # the subject's golden set + extracted prompt purely as data.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd base
          python3 -I tools/golden_lint.py ../subject/ai/golden/golden_set_v1.jsonl ../subject_prompt.txt


==============================================================================
===== FILE: .github/workflows/extraction-exam-dispatch.yml
==============================================================================

name: Extraction Golden-Set Exam — attended run

# The ONLY secret-bearing exam entry point — design v3 (evaluator r9 on the
# bootstrap PR tightened v2): the key never coexists with ANY untrusted
# code, attended or not. Mechanics:
#
#   * TRUSTED HARNESS: this job refuses to run unless dispatched on the
#     DEFAULT branch, and everything it executes — runner, provider,
#     scoring, thresholds, golden set, report writer — is that trusted
#     checkout's code.
#   * SUBJECT AS DATA: the commit under examination contributes exactly
#     one thing, its prompt TEXT, lifted from the subject commit by AST
#     parsing (tools/extract_prompt_text.py — never imported, never
#     executed) plus the candidate model id from the dispatch input.
#   * BINDING: the report artifact records model, prompt_sha256, and
#     subject_sha; the PR-side secretless verifier (extraction-eval.yml)
#     accepts evidence only when all three match ITS checkout — so a
#     forged/mismatched dispatch certifies nothing.
#
# Consequence, stated plainly: a PR that changes harness CODE (runner,
# provider, scoring, golden set) cannot be exam-certified until that
# harness change merges through the evaluator gate — harness first,
# subject second (the PR #11 "gate arms itself" bootstrap pattern).
#
# Required environment settings live in docs/ops/EXAM_ENVIRONMENT_SETUP.md
# (out-of-band checklist — the settings, not this file, are the secret
# boundary; this workflow only PROVES them before using the secret).
# workflow_dispatch is the attended-human property available on personal
# repos (environment required-reviewers is org-plan-only). Thresholds live
# in ai/golden_exam.py; the ANTHROPIC console spend cap bounds cost.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      subject_sha:
        description: "Commit SHA whose prompt is under examination (the PR head)"
        required: true
      model:
        description: "Candidate model id to examine (must equal the subject PR's routed model for release evidence)"
        required: true

concurrency:
  group: extraction-exam-dispatch
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  golden-exam-attended:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # The environment scopes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_EXAM to exam runs only (the
    # repo-wide key is never referenced here).
    environment: extraction-exam
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # The policy-proof step reads the environment + deployment-branch-
      # policy APIs (r21 blocker: contents alone 403s there, making the
      # gate unusable rather than fail-closed-on-misconfiguration).
      # Read-only scopes, no write of any kind.
      actions: read
      deployments: read
    steps:
      - name: Prove the environment's deployment-branch policy is ACTIVE (fail closed)
        # r19 blocker: the ref guard below is code inside whatever workflow
        # copy was dispatched — a branch copy could delete it and still
        # request this environment. The real boundary is GitHub's own
        # deployment-branch policy on the extraction-exam environment
        # (Settings -> Environments -> extraction-exam -> Deployment
        # branches: selected branches = the default branch only). This
        # step PROVES that policy is active before any secret-bearing
        # step; policy missing, unrestricted, or unverifiable = dead job.
        # No secrets are in scope here.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Strict proof (r20 blocker): ONLY a custom-branch policy whose
          # list is exactly the default branch counts. Protected-branches
          # mode is rejected (protected != default-only), and an empty or
          # unreadable list is rejected (an API hiccup must never read as
          # permission). One python block, one verdict, no lenient paths.
          : "${GH_TOKEN:?GH_TOKEN missing — cannot prove environment protection, failing closed}"
          curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/environments/extraction-exam" > env.json
          curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/environments/extraction-exam/deployment-branch-policies" > policies.json
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json, os, sys
          default = os.environ["DEFAULT_BRANCH"]
          try:
              env = json.load(open("env.json"))
              pol = json.load(open("policies.json"))
          except ValueError:
              print("::error::environment policy response unreadable — failing closed.")
              sys.exit(1)
          p = env.get("deployment_branch_policy")
          if not isinstance(p, dict) or p.get("protected_branches") is not False \
                  or p.get("custom_branch_policies") is not True:
              print("::error::extraction-exam must use a CUSTOM deployment-branch "
                    "policy (Selected branches), not protected-branches mode or "
                    "none — protected branches can include non-default branches. "
                    "Configure: Settings -> Environments -> extraction-exam -> "
                    "Deployment branches -> Selected branches. Failing closed.")
              sys.exit(1)
          names = sorted(b.get("name", "") for b in (pol.get("branch_policies") or []))
          if names != [default]:
              print(f"::error::extraction-exam branch policy list is {names!r}; "
                    f"it must be exactly ['{default}']. Failing closed.")
              sys.exit(1)
          print(f"environment deployment-branch policy verified: custom list == ['{default}']")
          PY

      - name: Refuse to run off the default branch (defense in depth; the policy above is the boundary)
        env:
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${DEFAULT_BRANCH:?default branch unresolved — failing closed}"
          if [ "$REF" != "refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
            echo "::error::attended exams run ONLY from the default branch (harness must be trusted code); dispatched ref was $REF. Dispatch on $DEFAULT_BRANCH and pass the PR head as subject_sha."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3, r9/r26 nit): pins must be VERIFIED upstream SHAs, and this sandboxed session cannot read actions/* to verify — tag stays until a networked session or the founder confirms the SHAs
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0        # need the subject commit reachable for data extraction

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3) — same constraint as checkout above
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # Dependency binding (r24, widened by r26): requirements.lock is the
      # FULL transitive resolution — its bytes are inside the report's
      # harness manifest hash, --no-deps means nothing outside it resolves,
      # the runner records EVERY installed distribution in the report, and
      # the PR-side verifier requires each locked entry to be recorded at
      # exactly its locked version — evidence names the complete dependency
      # set it ran under.
      - name: Install worker deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install --no-deps -r worker/requirements.lock

      - name: Extract SUBJECT data (prompt text via AST — never executed) and validate inputs
        env:
          SUBJECT_SHA: ${{ github.event.inputs.subject_sha }}
          RAW_MODEL: ${{ github.event.inputs.model }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          : "${SUBJECT_SHA:?subject_sha input missing — failing closed}"
          : "${RAW_MODEL:?model input missing — failing closed}"
          if ! [[ "$SUBJECT_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::subject_sha must be the FULL 40-character commit SHA (evidence later binds by exact equality to a PR head; abbreviations invite mismatches)."
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! [[ "$RAW_MODEL" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::model input is not a plausible model id (value redacted)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # Same-repo commits only (r15 nit): fork PR heads are not reachable
          # from origin and are OUT OF SCOPE for this solo private repo; fork
          # support would need an explicit subject repository input reviewed
          # on its own. Unreachable SHA = this fetch fails = fail closed.
          # Authenticated for THIS command only (r18 blocker: the checkout
          # deliberately persists no credentials, so a bare fetch fails on a
          # private repo — the gate could never mint evidence). The token is
          # scoped read-only and never written to git config on disk.
          : "${GH_TOKEN:?GH_TOKEN missing — cannot fetch the subject commit, failing closed}"
          AUTH_B64="$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GH_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)"
          git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $AUTH_B64" \
            fetch --no-tags origin "$SUBJECT_SHA"
          # ONLY the prompt file is taken from the subject, and only as text.
          git show "$SUBJECT_SHA:ai/prompts.py" > subject_prompts.py
          python3 tools/extract_prompt_text.py subject_prompts.py > subject_prompt.txt
          echo "EXAM_MODEL=$RAW_MODEL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "SUBJECT_SHA=$SUBJECT_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Run the golden-set exam (trusted harness, subject prompt as data)
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_EXAM }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${SUBJECT_SHA:?subject_sha input missing — failing closed}"
          if ! [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_EXAM is not configured as a secret of the 'extraction-exam' environment — the exam cannot run, and no-exam means no-pass (fail closed). Setup: Settings -> Environments -> extraction-exam -> Environment secrets."
            exit 1
          fi
          python -m ai.golden_exam --model "$EXAM_MODEL" \
            --prompt-file subject_prompt.txt \
            --subject-sha "$SUBJECT_SHA" \
            --report exam-report.json

      - name: Persist the exam report (evidence artifact)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4  # SHA-pin queued (TODOS P3) — same constraint as checkout above
        with:
          name: golden-exam-report-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: exam-report.json
          # Always error when the report is missing (r11 nit): whether the
          # exam passed, failed, or went invalid, forensics require the
          # report; the only report-less paths are pre-exam guard failures,
          # where a second explicit error on an already-red job is correct.
          if-no-files-found: error

name: import-licensed

# Deterministic licensed-feed import: Ticketmaster Discovery → licensed_event.
# NO AI, NO extraction spend (this is not the AI ingest cron; it does not run
# worker/run_once.py and is not covered by the arming-evidence binding). Runs on
# GitHub's runners, where egress reaches Ticketmaster (the dev sandbox's network
# policy blocks it). Triggered manually via workflow_dispatch.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_pages:
        description: "Ticketmaster pages to fetch (100 events/page; deep-paging caps ~9)"
        required: false
        default: "8"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: import-licensed
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  import:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install worker deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r worker/requirements.txt
      - name: Apply migration 0010 (idempotent) + import Ticketmaster CAPCOG events
        env:
          TICKETMASTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.TICKETMASTER_API_KEY }}
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN_RAW: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD }}
          MAX_PAGES: ${{ github.event.inputs.max_pages || '8' }}
        run: |
          : "${TICKETMASTER_API_KEY:?TICKETMASTER_API_KEY secret missing — add it in repo Settings → Secrets → Actions}"
          : "${MAX_PAGES:?max_pages missing — the fetch bound is required}"
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN="$(python3 tools/assemble_dsn.py)"
          export ONELIVE_DB_DSN
          python3 tools/apply_migration.py supabase/migrations/0010_licensed_feed_and_domains.sql
          python -m worker.importers.run_licensed_import --max-pages "$MAX_PAGES"

name: import-structured

# Deterministic STRUCTURED first-party feed import: the local moat sources
# (venue / university / library / civic / museum calendars that publish ICS or
# schema.org JSON-LD) → licensed_event. NO AI, NO extraction spend — this does
# NOT run worker/run_once.py and is NOT covered by the AI-ingest arming/dead-man
# binding (that governs the spend-capped Claude loop only). Runs on GitHub's
# runners, where egress reaches the venue sites (the dev sandbox's network policy
# blocks it), exactly like import-licensed.
#
# What it produces: rows in licensed_event marked 'confirmed' by construction (a
# venue publishing its OWN schedule is an authoritative anchor), CATEGORIZED by
# the shared resolver in authority order — the event's own schema.org @type
# first (a MusicEvent/ComedyEvent/LiteraryEvent → its true domain, even at a
# multi-purpose room), then the source's curated cultural_domain, then the title.
# licensed_event is already anon-readable (migration 0010, live — Ticketmaster
# rows already render), so these appear on /tonight through the SAME union read
# with no further grant.
#
# Migration: self-applies 0013 (registers the ics/jsonld providers in the
# licensed_event provider CHECK) idempotently before importing — mirroring how
# import-licensed self-applies 0010 — so running this workflow is the ONLY action
# needed to light up the local sources; no manual SQL step.
#
# Trigger: a twice-daily SCHEDULE plus manual workflow_dispatch. Per the charter
# Sentinel rule ("no scheduled loop ships without a dead-man ping"), the
# SCHEDULED path is watched by a healthchecks.io dead-man alarm: an "Assert
# dead-man period" step verifies the alarm's live config BEFORE the run (fail
# closed on any mismatch/missing key — the cron never runs unwatched), and the
# run pings success/fail so a silent stop raises the alarm within period+grace.
# The alarm is a SEPARATE check from the AI ingest one (its own ping-URL secret
# STRUCTURED_IMPORT_PING_URL + slug 'onelive-structured-import', period 1 day).
# The manual dispatch path is human-initiated and NOT gated by the alarm, so it
# can be run on demand (e.g. the first smoke run) before the healthcheck exists.

on:
  schedule:
    # Twice daily at 08:17 and 20:17 UTC (~03:17 and 15:17 America/Chicago) —
    # 12h apart, off the :00 congestion window (founder-directed 2026-07-25:
    # "should likely be 2x/day"). Deterministic, no AI spend. The two fires are
    # EVENLY spaced, so the dead-man period is 43200s (12h) —
    # EXPECTED_PERIOD_SECONDS below is bound to this cadence by the contract
    # test (which derives it from the hour list); change both together, and
    # keep the healthchecks.io check's period at 12h to match.
    - cron: "17 8,20 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      limit:
        description: "Max structured sources to fetch this run (a positive integer bound; required)"
        required: true
        default: "40"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: import-structured
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  import:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install worker deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r worker/requirements.txt

      - name: Assert dead-man period matches the schedule (scheduled runs only, fail closed)
        # Charter Sentinel rule: a live recurring job must not run with its alarm
        # config unverified. tools/assert_deadman_period.py (shared with the AI
        # ingest cron) reads THIS check's live period/grace via the founder-minted
        # READ-ONLY healthchecks key and refuses the run on mismatch, pause,
        # missing key, or a check the key cannot see. Gated to schedule events —
        # a manual dispatch is human-watched and may run before the check exists.
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL: ${{ secrets.STRUCTURED_IMPORT_PING_URL }}
          HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY_RO: ${{ secrets.HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY_RO }}
          DEADMAN_CHECK_SLUG: "onelive-structured-import"
          EXPECTED_PERIOD_SECONDS: "43200"
          MAX_GRACE_SECONDS: "7200"
        run: |
          python3 tools/assert_deadman_period.py

      - name: Dead-man START ping (scheduled runs only)
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          PING_URL: ${{ secrets.STRUCTURED_IMPORT_PING_URL }}
        run: |
          [ -n "$PING_URL" ] || exit 0
          curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 "$PING_URL/start" || true

      - name: Preconditions + validate the fetch bound (fail loud, never no-op)
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          # Untrusted dispatch input reaches the shell ONLY via env (never
          # ${{ }}-interpolated into run:) and must be a positive integer.
          LIMIT: ${{ github.event.inputs.limit }}
        run: |
          : "${LIMIT:?limit input missing — the fetch bound is required — failing closed}"
          if ! [[ "$LIMIT" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::limit must be a positive integer (the fetch bound is required; 0 is not allowed)."
            exit 1
          fi
          [ -n "$ONELIVE_DB_DSN" ] || {
            echo "::error::ONELIVE_DB_DSN secret missing — cannot import. Add it in repo Settings → Secrets → Actions."
            exit 1
          }

      - name: Validate DSN + register log mask (before anything else runs)
        # Same defense-in-depth as ingest.yml: assemble the credential from the
        # Supabase URI + password, URL-encoding the password, and register an
        # escaped ::add-mask:: so the assembled DSN stays redacted for the whole
        # job even on an unforeseen print path.
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN_RAW: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          python3 tools/assemble_dsn.py --mask-command

      - name: Apply migration 0013 (idempotent) + import the structured moat sources
        # The DB credential exists ONLY inside this step: assembled via command
        # substitution (never logged) and exported to this process alone — no
        # GITHUB_ENV, no step outputs.
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN_RAW: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD }}
          LIMIT: ${{ github.event.inputs.limit }}
        run: |
          : "${LIMIT:?limit input missing — the fetch bound is required — failing closed}"
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN="$(python3 tools/assemble_dsn.py)"
          export ONELIVE_DB_DSN
          python3 tools/apply_migration.py supabase/migrations/0013_structured_feed_provider.sql
          python -m worker.importers.run_structured_import --limit "$LIMIT"

      - name: Dead-man SUCCESS ping (scheduled runs only)
        # The load-bearing ping: a fresh success ping every period resets the
        # alarm. Its ABSENCE (job died, runner never fired, import failed before
        # here) is what raises the alarm within period+grace — so this must run
        # only on success.
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && success() }}
        env:
          PING_URL: ${{ secrets.STRUCTURED_IMPORT_PING_URL }}
        run: |
          [ -n "$PING_URL" ] || exit 0
          curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 "$PING_URL" || true

      - name: Dead-man FAIL ping (scheduled runs only)
        # Optional fast-path: signal failure immediately instead of waiting for
        # the missing-success-ping timeout. The alarm would fire either way.
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && failure() }}
        env:
          PING_URL: ${{ secrets.STRUCTURED_IMPORT_PING_URL }}
        run: |
          [ -n "$PING_URL" ] || exit 0
          curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 "$PING_URL/fail" || true

===== FILE: .github/workflows/ingest.yml
==============================================================================

name: Ingestion Run

# SPRINT Step 5. This workflow runs the real ingestion loop
# (fetch -> sensors -> extract -> gate3 -> candidate store; NEVER promotes —
# promotion is an authenticated human ops action only).
#
# ARMED 2026-07-21. Charter preconditions for scheduling a recurring loop
# (CLAUDE.md Sentinel rule; §14.3 budget caps): the spend-capped
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ONELIVE_DB_DSN, and ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL Actions
# secrets exist, founder-minted (the preconditions step below checks
# PRESENCE and fail-louds if any goes missing — presence is all a workflow
# can check; end-to-end CORRECTNESS is proven by the green pre-merge smoke
# run whose id is recorded in docs/FRICTION_LOG.md entry #3), and the
# Friction pre-work attack of the arming plan is logged and answered in
# that same entry (attacker: the non-Claude CI evaluator on the arming PR
# itself). Dead-man ping: worker/sentinel.py wraps the run in
# start/success/fail pings, and the alarm's configuration is asserted
# MECHANICALLY before every run (PR #43 r11 — prose confirmation was
# correctly rejected for a live cron): the "Assert dead-man period"
# step reads the check's live period/grace through the founder-minted
# READ-ONLY healthchecks API key and fails CLOSED on any mismatch,
# pause, or unreadable state — the loop never runs unwatched. R-020
# tracks this contract; tests/test_ingest_workflow_contract.py derives
# the expected period from the cron line itself, so cadence, declared
# period, and the live check cannot drift apart silently.
#
# Budget shape (§14.3): `schedule` events run with a fixed 10-source
# ceiling (keyed on event_name below — dispatch inputs don't exist on
# schedule events); with least-recently-attempted rotation in
# worker/run_once.py, 10/run x 72 slots/day gives capacity to visit the
# ~230-source catalog ~3x daily instead of starving the tail. Manual
# dispatch still requires an explicit ceiling and FAILS LOUD without one
# — the fixed fallback never applies outside `schedule`.
# AI-SPEND BOUND (R-043): the source ceiling caps PAGES; multi-event fan-out
# makes one extraction call per event block, so the AI-call bound per run is
# max_sources x EXTRACT_MAX_EVENTS_PER_PAGE (worker/ai_extract.py, default 50),
# i.e. <= 500 extraction calls/run at the fixed 10-source schedule ceiling.
# The Anthropic console monthly cap is the hard backstop above both.

on:
  schedule:
    # Every 20 minutes (founder-directed 2026-07-21: "accelerate the
    # ingestion to every 15 or 20 minutes" — spend escalation is the
    # founder's own; ~3x hourly-cadence cost, bounded by the source ceiling x
    # the per-page extraction cap (R-043) and the console monthly cap). Minutes chosen off the
    # :00 congestion window where GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs. A
    # missed run is caught by the dead-man check (period 20min + grace),
    # not by log-reading.
    # Minutes shifted 7,27,47 -> 9,29,49 on 2026-07-22 (founder-approved)
    # to prompt scheduler re-registration; cadence unchanged (every 20
    # min). Registration cannot be proven pre-merge (schedules register
    # only from the default branch): the success criterion is the first
    # schedule-event run id (docs/RECORD.md R-008), and continued absence
    # is detected FAIL-CLOSED by the dead-man alarm within period+grace
    # (~30 min) of the last ping. Incident record: R-008 row, 2026-07-22.
    - cron: "9,29,49 * * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_sources:
        description: "Budget ceiling: max sources this run (required; §14.3)"
        required: true
        default: "10"
      report_flips:
        description: "Set 1 to print the dead-man check's 24h flip history after the assertion (R-023 PATH A probe; read-only, additive)"
        required: false
        default: "0"

concurrency:
  group: ingest
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  ingest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Validate the budget ceiling input (fail closed, never interpolate)
        env:
          # Untrusted dispatch input reaches the shell ONLY via env (never
          # ${{ }}-interpolated into run: — shell-injection surface) and must
          # be a positive integer; 0/negative is rejected here AND in
          # run_once.py (defense in depth, evaluator finding PR #12 round 1).
          # The fixed 10-source ceiling applies to `schedule` events ONLY
          # (keyed on event_name, which callers cannot influence) — every
          # other event type, including manual/API dispatch with a missing
          # or empty input, still FAILS LOUD below. A bare `||` fallback
          # would have silently substituted 10 for any empty dispatch input,
          # weakening the fail-closed budget contract (evaluator finding,
          # PR #43 round 1).
          MAX_SOURCES: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '10' || github.event.inputs.max_sources }}
        run: |
          : "${MAX_SOURCES:?max_sources input missing — the budget ceiling is required — failing closed}"
          # [[ =~ ]] validates the WHOLE string (POSIX ERE, not line-oriented
          # like grep — a newline-smuggled second line cannot pass), and the
          # raw value is never echoed into an annotation (log-command
          # injection surface) — evaluator nits, PR #12 round 2.
          if ! [[ "$MAX_SOURCES" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::max_sources must be a positive integer (invalid value redacted — check the run input). The budget ceiling is required and fails closed; 0 does not mean uncapped."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Preconditions (fail loud, never no-op)
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL: ${{ secrets.ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL }}
        run: |
          missing=""
          [ -n "$ONELIVE_DB_DSN" ] || missing="$missing ONELIVE_DB_DSN"
          [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ] || missing="$missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
          [ -n "$ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL" ] || missing="$missing ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL"
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::error::Ingestion refused — missing Actions secret(s):$missing. Minting keys is founder-crucial; the Anthropic key requires a console spend cap FIRST (§14.3). See docs/SPRINT_LIVE_SITE.md Step 5."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Assert dead-man period matches the armed cadence (R-020, fail closed)
        # PR #43 r11: a live recurring cron must not run with its Sentinel
        # alarm config unverified. tools/assert_deadman_period.py (tested)
        # reads the check's LIVE period/grace via the founder-minted
        # READ-ONLY healthchecks API key and refuses the run on mismatch,
        # pause, missing key, unreadable API, or a check the key cannot
        # see — unwatched is not an option. EXPECTED_PERIOD_SECONDS is
        # bound to the cron line above by
        # tests/test_ingest_workflow_contract.py, which recomputes it from
        # the cron minutes — editing one without the other fails the suite.
        env:
          ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL: ${{ secrets.ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL }}
          HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY_RO: ${{ secrets.HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY_RO }}
          # The dead-man check, DECLARED by name/slug (primary match path —
          # read-only keys don't expose ping URLs and the unique_key hash
          # derivation proved undocumented; declaration beats inference).
          DEADMAN_CHECK_SLUG: "onelive-ingestion"
          EXPECTED_PERIOD_SECONDS: "1200"
          MAX_GRACE_SECONDS: "600"
          # R-023 PATH A probe: dispatch-only, read-only, additive — runs
          # AFTER the assertion passes and only prints the check's flip
          # history (did the alarm actually fire?). Schedule events never
          # set it (callers cannot influence event_name), so the armed
          # cadence's behavior is unchanged.
          REPORT_FLIPS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.report_flips || '0' }}
        run: |
          python3 tools/assert_deadman_period.py

      - name: Validate DSN + register log mask (before anything installs)
        # Founder ergonomics (2026-07-14): the Supabase Connect panel emits a
        # URI with a literal [YOUR-PASSWORD] placeholder. tools/assemble_dsn
        # .py (unit-tested) splices in ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD, URL-encoding it.
        # Defense in depth (evaluator, PR #19 rounds 1-2), BOTH layers:
        #   SCOPE — the assembled credential is exported only inside the run
        #     step below, never via GITHUB_ENV/outputs, so pip install and
        #     other steps never see it;
        #   MASKING — the URL-encoded DSN differs from both GitHub secrets,
        #     so auto-redaction misses it; --mask-command registers a
        #     properly ESCAPED ::add-mask:: ('%'→'%25' first — the escaping
        #     hole was round 1's leak) so even an unforeseen failure path
        #     that prints the environment stays redacted for the whole job.
        # This step also fail-louds on misconfig before deps install.
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN_RAW: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          python3 tools/assemble_dsn.py --mask-command

      - name: Install worker deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r worker/requirements.txt

      - name: Run the loop once (capped, dead-man pinged)
        # The DB credential exists ONLY inside this step: assembled here via
        # command substitution (never logged — the script prints nothing but
        # the DSN, captured silently) and exported to the worker process
        # alone. No GITHUB_ENV, no step outputs, no add-mask escaping
        # surface.
        env:
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN_RAW: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_DSN }}
          ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ONELIVE_DB_PASSWORD }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL: ${{ secrets.ORCHESTRATOR_PING_URL }}
          SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_DSN }}
          # IDENTICAL expression to the validation step (schedule-only fixed
          # ceiling; dispatch stays fail-loud) — both steps must agree or the
          # validated value wouldn't be the executed value.
          MAX_SOURCES: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '10' || github.event.inputs.max_sources }}
        run: |
          : "${MAX_SOURCES:?max_sources input missing — the budget ceiling is required — failing closed}"
          ONELIVE_DB_DSN="$(python3 tools/assemble_dsn.py)"
          export ONELIVE_DB_DSN
          python worker/run_once.py --real --max-sources "$MAX_SOURCES"

      - name: Persist the replay log (audit trail)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: replay-log-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: var/replay/
          # A successful real run MUST leave a replay audit trail — absence on
          # success is a failure. After an earlier failed step, absence is
          # expected and merely warned (the failure is already red).
          if-no-files-found: ${{ job.status == 'success' && 'error' || 'warn' }}

  workflow_dispatch:

name: Weekly Source Catalog Backfill

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 14 * * 1'   # Mondays 9am America/Chicago (14:00 UTC in summer)
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  group: source-backfill
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  backfill:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Model resolved via the cost-routing policy (docs/MODEL_ROUTING.md),
      # never hardcoded — catalog research is a Standard-tier task. The
      # substitution runs in its own assignment (not inside echo) so a router
      # failure fails THIS STEP under `bash -e`, never becoming `model=`.
      - name: Resolve model (cost routing)
        id: route
        run: |
          model="$(python3 tools/model_router.py standard)"
          test -n "$model"
          echo "model=$model" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          model: ${{ steps.route.outputs.model }}
          max_turns: 12
          allowed_tools: "git,gh pr,web_search"
          prompt: |
            Read STATE.md and the source catalog file (ranks 42-118 are TODO placeholders).
            Research and propose 5-10 real Austin nightlife/event data sources
            (ticketing platforms, venue calendars, community/social sources, newsletters,
            city/municipal event listings) that aren't already in the catalog.
            Fill in real names, URLs, and a reasonable priority_score using the existing formula.
            Open a PR with your additions. Do not merge — this always needs founder review.

===== FILE: .github/workflows/trust-gate.yml
==============================================================================

name: Trust Gate

# Deterministic, hermetic trust-invariant checks. Replaces the AI PR-review
# action (which required the Claude GitHub App and gave non-deterministic
# results). A trust INVARIANT must be enforced by a check that returns the same
# answer every time — so it is code in-repo (tools/trust_gate.py), not an AI.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  push:
    branches: [master]

concurrency:
  group: trust-gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  trust-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # actions:read powers the arming-evidence API authentication in
      # tests/test_arming_smoke_binding.py (PR #43 r21: self-authored run
      # evidence must be machine-verified against the Actions API — run
      # exists, succeeded, on the recorded SHA, artifact matches).
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Full history (stage-6 r2): trust_gate's golden-set content
          # binding hashes the set AT THE CERTIFIED SUBJECT COMMIT from git
          # history — a shallow clone would fail that check closed.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install worker + api deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r worker/requirements.txt -r api/requirements.txt pytest

      - name: Trust invariants (no dynamic SQL; ads isolated; AI never promotes)
        run: python tools/trust_gate.py

      - name: Test suite
        env:
          # The arming-evidence binding test verifies the recorded smoke
          # run against the live Actions API here — REQUIRED in this job
          # (fail closed if the token is missing), because trust-gate is a
          # required check with full history: the authoritative venue for
          # both halves of the binding proof (PR #43 r21).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ARMING_SMOKE_VERIFY: "required"
        run: python -m pytest -q

      - name: Extraction eval harness (precision/recall/F1/hallucination)
        run: |
          # eval_harness scores extraction quality against the golden set. It is
          # a module; running it as a script executes its self-check. If it has
          # no __main__ yet, importing it must at least succeed (no import-time
          # regressions) — fail loudly if even that breaks.
          python -c "import ai.eval_harness as e; print('eval_harness import OK:', [n for n in dir(e) if not n.startswith('_')][:8])"



# TESTS


==============================================================================
===== FILE: tests/conftest.py
==============================================================================

"""Shared pytest fixtures for OneLive.

Most tests here are pure-logic and need no database. Tests that DO need a live
Postgres are marked with `@pytest.mark.dbintegration` and use the `db_conn`
fixture, which skips automatically unless ONELIVE_TEST_DB_DSN is set.

    export ONELIVE_TEST_DB_DSN="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/onelive_test"
    pytest -m dbintegration        # run only DB integration tests
    pytest -m "not dbintegration"  # run only pure-logic tests (default in CI)
"""
import os
import sys

import pytest

# Ensure the repo root is importable (so `import worker.*` / `import api.*` work
# regardless of where pytest is invoked from).
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def pytest_configure(config):
    config.addinivalue_line(
        "markers",
        "dbintegration: test requires a live Postgres (set ONELIVE_TEST_DB_DSN)",
    )
    config.addinivalue_line(
        "markers",
        "perf: performance/timing benchmark (skipped by default; run explicitly "
        "with `pytest -m perf`, see tools/profile_target.py and docs/TESTS.md)",
    )
    config.addinivalue_line(
        "markers",
        "visual: visual-regression check against tests/visual_baselines/ "
        "(skipped by default; requires a booted app, see tools/visual_regression.py)",
    )


def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
    """perf and visual tests are opt-in only: they require either a real
    timing budget (perf) or a booted app + baseline images (visual), neither
    of which belongs in the default fast/pure-logic suite that runs on every
    commit. Skip them UNLESS the run explicitly selected them via `-m perf`,
    `-m visual`, or a combination that mentions them (e.g. `-m "perf or visual"`)
    -- mirrors how `-m dbintegration` is used to opt IN to DB tests elsewhere
    in this file, just via auto-skip instead of a fixture, since there's no
    natural single fixture every perf/visual test shares.
    """
    markexpr = config.getoption("markexpr", default="") or ""
    for opt_in_marker in ("perf", "visual"):
        if opt_in_marker in markexpr:
            continue  # this run explicitly asked for these; don't skip them
        skip_marker = pytest.mark.skip(
            reason=f"'{opt_in_marker}' tests are opt-in only; run with `pytest -m {opt_in_marker}`"
        )
        for item in items:
            if opt_in_marker in item.keywords:
                item.add_marker(skip_marker)


@pytest.fixture
def db_conn():
    dsn = os.getenv("ONELIVE_TEST_DB_DSN")
    if not dsn:
        pytest.skip("ONELIVE_TEST_DB_DSN not set; skipping DB integration test")
    psycopg2 = pytest.importorskip("psycopg2")
    conn = psycopg2.connect(dsn)
    try:
        yield conn
    finally:
        conn.rollback()
        conn.close()

===== FILE: tests/test_acquisition_toolkit.py
==============================================================================

"""Proof tests for the shared, learning acquisition toolkit (brain/acquisition.py).

Greppable summary: each test PROVES one property the founder asked to see —
recipes and techniques round-trip through the brain store (durable + shared),
record_outcome improves a recipe's reliability + median_yield and a technique's
success stats, repeated empty yield flips needs_rediscovery, a login/paywall
bypass recipe is HARD-REJECTED, best_technique returns the higher-success
method, and the brain's four write invariants still hold (a recipe/technique
claim cannot enter the graph without a Source and a run).

Pure-logic tests: no database, no network.
"""
import pathlib

import pytest

from brain import store
from brain.graph import Graph, GraphInvariantError
from brain.schema import Claim, EdgeType, NodeType
from brain.acquisition import (
    AcquisitionError,
    AcquisitionRecipe,
    AcquisitionTechnique,
    AcquisitionToolkit,
    _assert_recipe_legal,
)
from brain.seed_acquisition import recipe_from_source, seed, technique_library


# --- helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------
def _kit_with_recipe(**over):
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    base = dict(source_id="mohawk", source_name="Mohawk", calendar_url="https://m/cal",
                access_method="ics_feed", structured_format="ics", reliability=0.5,
                confidence=0.5)
    base.update(over)
    kit.register_recipe(AcquisitionRecipe(**base), run_id="run-1",
                        source_uri="catalog.json")
    return kit


def _seed_techniques(kit):
    for t in technique_library():
        kit.register_technique(t, run_id="run-1")


# --- recipe read/write round-trips through the brain store --------------------
def test_recipe_roundtrips_through_the_store(tmp_path: pathlib.Path):
    kit = _kit_with_recipe(access_method="jsonld", structured_format="jsonld",
                           median_yield=0.0)
    kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="jsonld",
                       technique=None, yield_count=12, success=True, at=100.0)

    path = tmp_path / "acq.jsonl"
    kit.save(path)
    # A FRESH toolkit that never saw the original reads it back off disk.
    reloaded = AcquisitionToolkit.load(path)
    r = reloaded.recipe_for("mohawk")
    assert r is not None
    assert r.source_id == "mohawk"
    assert r.access_method == "jsonld"
    assert r.median_yield == 12.0
    assert r.last_yield == 12
    # Full-state identity: serialising both graphs yields identical bytes.
    assert store.dumps(reloaded.g) == store.dumps(kit.g)


def test_unknown_source_reads_as_none():
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    assert kit.recipe_for("never_seen") is None
    assert kit.technique("never_seen") is None


# --- record_outcome improves reliability + median_yield + technique stats -----
def test_record_outcome_improves_reliability_and_median_yield():
    kit = _kit_with_recipe(reliability=0.5, median_yield=0.0)
    r0 = kit.recipe_for("mohawk")
    r1 = kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed",
                            technique=None, yield_count=10, success=True, at=1.0)
    assert r1.reliability > r0.reliability          # a success raised reliability
    assert r1.median_yield == 10.0                  # median of [10]
    assert r1.successes == 1 and r1.attempts == 1
    r2 = kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed",
                            technique=None, yield_count=20, success=True, at=2.0)
    assert r2.median_yield == 15.0                  # median of [10, 20]
    assert r2.reliability > r1.reliability
    # Each write superseded the prior state claim (invariant 4): exactly one
    # live recipe claim mentions the entity, and the history is retained.
    entity = kit._entity("acquisition_recipe", "mohawk")
    live = [e for e in kit.g.edges_of(entity.id)
            if e.edge_type is EdgeType.MENTIONS and e.dst == entity.id
            and not kit.g.get(e.src).superseded]
    assert len(live) == 1
    superseded = [e for e in kit.g.edges_of(entity.id)
                  if e.edge_type is EdgeType.MENTIONS and e.dst == entity.id
                  and kit.g.get(e.src).superseded]
    assert len(superseded) >= 2                     # seed + first outcome retained


def test_record_outcome_updates_technique_stats():
    kit = _kit_with_recipe()
    _seed_techniques(kit)
    t0 = kit.technique("parse-ics-feed")
    kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed",
                       technique="parse-ics-feed", yield_count=5, success=True, at=1.0)
    t1 = kit.technique("parse-ics-feed")
    assert t1.attempts == t0.attempts + 1
    assert t1.successes == t0.successes + 1
    assert t1.effective_success_rate() > t0.effective_success_rate()


def test_record_outcome_on_unknown_source_raises():
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    with pytest.raises(AcquisitionError):
        kit.record_outcome("ghost", run_id="run-1", method="plain_http",
                           technique=None, yield_count=1, success=True)


def test_record_outcome_naming_unknown_technique_raises():
    kit = _kit_with_recipe()
    with pytest.raises(AcquisitionError):
        kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed",
                           technique="no-such-technique", yield_count=3, success=True)


# --- repeated empty -> needs_rediscovery flips (moved-page trigger) -----------
def test_repeated_empty_flips_needs_rediscovery():
    kit = _kit_with_recipe(confidence=0.9)
    kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed", technique=None,
                       yield_count=0, success=False, at=1.0)
    assert kit.recipe_for("mohawk").needs_rediscovery is False   # one empty: not yet
    r = kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed", technique=None,
                           yield_count=0, success=False, at=2.0)
    assert r.needs_rediscovery is True                            # two in a row: flip
    assert r.consecutive_empty == 2
    assert r.confidence < 0.9                                     # confidence dropped


def test_success_after_empties_clears_rediscovery():
    kit = _kit_with_recipe()
    for t in (1.0, 2.0):
        kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed", technique=None,
                           yield_count=0, success=False, at=t)
    assert kit.recipe_for("mohawk").needs_rediscovery is True
    r = kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed", technique=None,
                           yield_count=7, success=True, at=3.0)
    assert r.needs_rediscovery is False
    assert r.consecutive_empty == 0


def test_success_with_zero_yield_is_not_effective():
    # A mechanical "success" that returned zero events did NOT really succeed.
    kit = _kit_with_recipe()
    kit.record_outcome("mohawk", run_id="run-1", method="ics_feed", technique=None,
                       yield_count=0, success=True, at=1.0)
    r = kit.recipe_for("mohawk")
    assert r.successes == 0
    assert r.consecutive_empty == 1


# --- a recipe can NEVER encode a disallowed method ----------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [
    dict(access_method="plain_http", plan_note="log in and scrape the member calendar"),
    dict(access_method="plain_http", plan_note="bypass the paywall to read events"),
    dict(access_method="plain_http", plan_note="use stored credentials to sign in"),
    dict(access_method="plain_http", segmentation_hint="solve the captcha then read"),
    dict(access_method="scrape_login"),          # unknown/forbidden method itself
    dict(access_method="plain_http", robots_ok=False),  # ignoring robots
])
def test_bypass_recipe_is_hard_rejected(bad):
    recipe = AcquisitionRecipe(source_id="evil", **bad)
    with pytest.raises(AcquisitionError):
        _assert_recipe_legal(recipe)
    # And it can never be stored through the toolkit either.
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    with pytest.raises(AcquisitionError):
        kit.register_recipe(recipe, run_id="run-1")


def test_legal_rails_note_does_not_false_reject():
    # A recipe whose tos_note/explicitly_disallowed MENTION "login_scraping" as a
    # GUARDRAIL (what NOT to do) is fine — only ACTION fields are scanned.
    recipe = AcquisitionRecipe(
        source_id="mohawk", access_method="ics_feed", structured_format="ics",
        plan_note="read the offered ICS feed",
        tos_note="respect source policy; explicitly disallowed: login_scraping",
        explicitly_disallowed=["login_scraping"])
    _assert_recipe_legal(recipe)  # must NOT raise
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    kit.register_recipe(recipe, run_id="run-1")
    assert kit.recipe_for("mohawk") is not None


def test_seed_maps_catalog_without_illegal_recipes():
    # Every catalog-derived recipe passes the legal rail and uses a safe method.
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    summary = seed(kit)
    assert summary["recipes"] > 60
    for r in kit.all_recipes():
        _assert_recipe_legal(r)                 # raises if any is a bypass
        assert r.robots_ok is True
    # Re-seed is idempotent: no new recipes/techniques the second time.
    summary2 = seed(kit)
    assert summary2["recipes_new"] == 0
    assert summary2["techniques_new"] == 0


def test_seed_marks_benchmark_channels_not_automated():
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    seed(kit)
    bing = kit.recipe_for("bing_search")        # a benchmark-only source
    assert bing is not None
    assert bing.automated_ok is False


# --- best_technique returns the higher-success technique ----------------------
def test_best_technique_prefers_higher_success():
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    _seed_techniques(kit)
    # Both parse-jsonld-graph-event (prior .7) and detect-js-shell-then-render
    # (prior .6) apply to the 'squarespace' signal; jsonld wins initially.
    assert kit.best_technique("squarespace").name == "parse-jsonld-graph-event"
    # Record two render successes -> its observed rate overtakes jsonld's prior.
    kit.register_recipe(AcquisitionRecipe(source_id="sq", access_method="js_render",
                                          plan_note="render then parse"),
                        run_id="run-1")
    for t in (1.0, 2.0):
        kit.record_outcome("sq", run_id="run-1", method="js_render",
                           technique="detect-js-shell-then-render",
                           yield_count=9, success=True, at=t)
    assert kit.best_technique("squarespace").name == "detect-js-shell-then-render"


def test_best_technique_unknown_signal_is_none():
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    _seed_techniques(kit)
    assert kit.best_technique("no_such_signal") is None


# --- the 4 brain write invariants still hold ----------------------------------
def test_recipe_claim_without_source_raises_brain_invariant():
    # A recipe/technique claim is a brain Claim: writing one with no Source and
    # no inference flag violates brain invariant 1 and raises loudly.
    g = Graph()
    with pytest.raises(GraphInvariantError):
        g.add_claim(Claim(text='{"kind": "acquisition_recipe"}',
                          source_id=None, inference=False))


def test_recipe_write_requires_a_run():
    # This module's own rule: every recipe write is bound to an AgentRun. A
    # blank run_id is refused (provenance cannot be dropped).
    kit = AcquisitionToolkit()
    with pytest.raises(AcquisitionError):
        kit.register_recipe(AcquisitionRecipe(source_id="x", access_method="plain_http"),
                            run_id="")


def test_stored_recipe_claim_cites_a_source_and_binds_the_run():
    # Structural proof: the stored recipe claim carries a DERIVED_FROM edge to a
    # Source (invariant 1) AND a DERIVED_FROM edge to the AgentRun that learned
    # it (this module's binding), so provenance is fully traversable.
    kit = _kit_with_recipe()
    entity = kit._entity("acquisition_recipe", "mohawk")
    claim = kit._current_claim(entity.id)
    assert claim is not None
    derived = [e for e in kit.g.edges_of(claim.id)
               if e.edge_type is EdgeType.DERIVED_FROM and e.src == claim.id]
    dst_types = {kit.g.get(e.dst).node_type for e in derived}
    assert NodeType.SOURCE in dst_types
    assert NodeType.AGENT_RUN in dst_types


def test_recipe_from_source_prefers_structured_feed():
    # A catalog row offering an ICS feed maps to the cheap structured method,
    # not a plain HTML scrape (cost discipline + authoritative anchor).
    row = {"id": "v1", "name": "Venue One", "base_url": "https://v1.example/calendar",
           "access_method": "public_web_or_ics", "access_reliability": 0.8,
           "credibility_weight": 0.85,
           "allowed": ["public_calendar_pages", "ics_feed_if_offered"],
           "explicitly_disallowed": ["login_scraping"]}
    r = recipe_from_source(row)
    assert r.access_method == "ics_feed"
    assert r.structured_format == "ics"
    assert r.calendar_url_is_homepage is False       # URL has a /calendar path
    _assert_recipe_legal(r)

===== FILE: tests/test_adversarial_review.py
==============================================================================

"""Tests for tools/adversarial_review.py — the non-Claude evaluator gate.

Hermetic: no network, no OpenAI key. The transport (`_post_json`) is
monkeypatched; git interaction is avoided via --diff-file. Proves the verdict
parse is strict (ambiguity = hard failure, never a pass), the skip-without-key
path stays loud but non-blocking unless --require, and exit codes follow the
tools/README.md 0/1/2 convention.
"""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys

import pytest

_TOOL_PATH = (
    pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "tools" / "adversarial_review.py"
)
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("adversarial_review", _TOOL_PATH)
ar = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
sys.modules["adversarial_review"] = ar
_spec.loader.exec_module(ar)

_DIFF = "diff --git a/x.py b/x.py\n+print('hi')\n"


def _diff_file(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "change.patch"
    p.write_text(_DIFF)
    return str(p)


def _fake_response(text):
    return {"choices": [{"message": {"content": text}}]}


def test_parse_verdict_approve_and_request_changes():
    assert ar.parse_verdict("looks good\nVERDICT: APPROVE") == ar.APPROVE
    assert (
        ar.parse_verdict("a.py:3 — bug\nVERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES")
        == ar.REQUEST_CHANGES
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "no verdict at all",
        "VERDICT: APPROVE\nVERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES",  # two verdicts = ambiguous
        "VERDICT: MAYBE",
        # Evaluator finding (PR #11 round 1): the verdict must be the FINAL
        # line — trailing prose could contradict or launder it.
        "VERDICT: APPROVE\nbut actually I have grave concerns",
    ],
)
def test_parse_verdict_rejects_ambiguity(text):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ar.parse_verdict(text)


def test_require_mode_refuses_truncated_diff(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    """Evaluator finding (PR #11 round 1): a partial diff is not a review —
    in --require (CI) mode an over-limit diff is a hard failure, never a
    silent truncation the reviewer can't see past."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        ar, "_post_json", lambda *a, **k: _fake_response("fine\nVERDICT: APPROVE")
    )
    big = tmp_path / "big.patch"
    big.write_text("x" * 500)
    args = ["--diff-file", str(big), "--max-diff-bytes", "100"]
    assert ar.main(args + ["--require"]) == 2
    assert "truncated" in capsys.readouterr().err
    # Without --require (local/advisory use) the same diff truncates and runs.
    assert ar.main(args) == 0

    assert ar._TRUNCATION_MARKER.strip() in truncated

def test_unset_model_env_uses_default(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Truly-UNSET model/base-url env means the documented defaults."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", raising=False)
    sent = {}

    def _capture(url, payload, api_key, timeout=300):

        sent["model"] = payload["model"]

    monkeypatch.setattr(ar, "_post_json", _capture)

def test_empty_model_env_var_hard_fails(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    """Fail-closed (supersedes the first-live-run fallback behavior): a
    PRESENT-but-empty OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL is a misconfiguration on the
    trust-critical review path and must hard-fail, never silently mean the
    default. The workflow expresses 'unset' by not exporting the var."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", raising=False)

    def _explode(*a, **k):
        raise AssertionError("no API call may happen on misconfigured env")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ar, "_post_json", _explode)
    for empty in ("", "   "):
        monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL", empty)
        assert ar.main(["--diff-file", _diff_file(tmp_path)]) == 2
        assert "set but empty" in capsys.readouterr().err
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "")
    assert ar.main(["--diff-file", _diff_file(tmp_path)]) == 2


def test_generator_family_review_model_hard_fails(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    """Trust invariant (charter §0.2), enforced at the reviewer's OWN entry
    point: a Claude/Anthropic model in OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL means the generator
    would grade its own work — hard fail (exit 2) BEFORE any API call."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "test-key")

    def _explode(*a, **k):
        raise AssertionError("no API call may happen with a generator-family model")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ar, "_post_json", _explode)
    for bad in ("claude-opus-4-8", "Claude-Sonnet-4-6", "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"):
        monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_REVIEW_MODEL", bad)
        assert ar.main(["--diff-file", _diff_file(tmp_path)]) == 2
        assert "write/grade separation" in capsys.readouterr().err


def test_http_error_body_is_surfaced(monkeypatch):
    """Regression (first live CI run): a bare 'HTTP Error 400' is undiagnosable;
    the API's error body must reach the failure message."""
    import io
    import urllib.error

    def _boom(req, timeout):
        raise urllib.error.HTTPError(
            "https://api.example/v1/chat/completions", 400, "Bad Request",
            hdrs=None, fp=io.BytesIO(b'{"error": {"message": "you must provide a model"}}'),
        )

    monkeypatch.setattr(ar.urllib.request, "urlopen", _boom)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="you must provide a model"):
        ar._post_json("https://api.example/v1/chat/completions", {}, "k")
